  unknown_handle (3)
      `profile` names no profile Handle in this Workspace. `candidates` lists profile
      Handles, newest first.
  wrong_handle_kind (2)
      `profile` is a Handle of another kind.
  unknown_column (3)
      `column` is not a column of the profile. `candidates` lists close matches.
  invalid_argument (2)
      An argument has the wrong type or is out of its range.
  incompatible_artifact (6)
      Another library format version wrote `profile`.
  invalid_setting (2)
      A Workspace Setting is invalid. The message names it and its source.

See Also:
  describe-target: Read a target's problem type and statistics.
  missingness: Read which columns go missing together.
  profile: Make the profile Handle and its Dataset Digest.

Cost: reads only stored records; it does not grow with the data.

Example:
  $ dataforge load --path train.csv
  {...,"frame":"frame_7f3a9c2e",...}
  $ dataforge profile --frame frame_7f3a9c2e --targets income
  {...,"profile":"profile_1b2c3d4e",...}
  $ dataforge top-associations --profile profile_1b2c3d4e --column income
  {...,"profile":"profile_1b2c3d4e","total":1,"offset":0,"pairs":{"fields":["column_a","column_b","metric","value","near_redundant"],"rows":[["income","city","eta_squared",...,true]]},...}
commands.value-summary:
usage: dataforge value-summary --profile <string> --column <string> [--k <integer>]

Read one column's top values, rare labels, bounds and percentiles off a profile Handle.

Use when:
  Call this to see a column's actual values: to spot sentinels such as `-999` or `"?"`
  that stand for missing values, to learn the labels a categorical column uses, or to
  check a column's range. These are cell values, so each one is in a Literal Field;
  every other detail Operation holds none. To read a spotted sentinel as missing, call
  `profile` again with it in `sentinels`. It reads the stored profile only, so it is
  cheap and never recomputes.

Flags (a flag left out is null, which means its default):
  --profile <string>, required
      A profile Handle, such as `profile_7f3a9c2e`.
  --column <string>, required
      A column of the profile.
  --k <integer>, optional
      Most entries in each list, from 1 to 20. Null means 20. Constraints: at least 1;
      at most 20.

Returns ValueSummaryResult, as one JSON object:
  profile: string
      The profile Handle read.
  column: string
      The column summarised.
  semantic_type: one of numeric|categorical|datetime|boolean|text|identifier
      The column's semantic type; null when it was skipped.
  cardinality: integer
      Number of distinct non-missing values; null when skipped.
  top_values: table of (value, count, share)
      The most common values, most common first. The profile keeps up to 10 for a
      categorical, boolean or whole-number column and none for a continuous one;
      `omitted` counts the rest.
  rare_labels: list of true|false or integer or number or string or null
      Labels of a categorical column rarer than
      `thresholds.categorical.stratification_rare_threshold_pct` of `profile`, most
      common first. A Literal Field.
  bounds: object
      The smallest and largest value of a numeric or datetime column; else null.
  median: true|false or integer or number or string or null
      The median of a numeric column; else null. A Literal Field.
  mode: true|false or integer or number or string or null
      The most common value; null for a datetime or text column. A Literal Field.
  percentiles: table of (percentile, value)
      Percentiles of a numeric column, lowest first; empty for any other type.
  Every result also has `warnings` (caveats; read them first) and `omitted` (cut lists,
  each naming the command that returns the rest).

Errors (Error Code, exit code):
  unknown_handle (3)
      `profile` names no profile Handle in this Workspace. `candidates` lists profile
      Handles, newest first.
  wrong_handle_kind (2)
      `profile` is a Handle of another kind.
  unknown_column (3)
      `column` is not a column of the profile. `candidates` lists close matches.
  invalid_argument (2)
      An argument has the wrong type or is out of its range.
  incompatible_artifact (6)
      Another library format version wrote `profile`.
  invalid_setting (2)
      A Workspace Setting is invalid. The message names it and its source.

See Also:
  describe-columns: Read a column's statistics without cell values.
  profile: Declare sentinels and make the profile Handle.

Cost: reads only stored records; it does not grow with the data.

Example:
  $ dataforge load --path train.csv
  {...,"frame":"frame_7f3a9c2e",...}
  $ dataforge profile --frame frame_7f3a9c2e
  {...,"profile":"profile_1b2c3d4e",...}
  $ dataforge value-summary --profile profile_1b2c3d4e --column city --k 2
  {...,"column":"city","semantic_type":"categorical","cardinality":3,"top_values":{"fields":["value","count","share"],"rows":[["north",2,...],["south",2,...]]},...}

query-frame.filter:
filter: list of list of object, optional
  An OR of up to 5 AND-lists, each of 1 to 10 `{"column": ..., "op": ..., "value": ...}`
  predicates. A row matches when every predicate of any one list passes. The ops are
  `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `gt`, `ge`, `in` (up to 100 values), `not_in`, `is_null` and
  `not_null`. A null or NaN cell passes only `is_null`. A declared sentinel is a value
  like any other, so `is_null` can disagree with the profile's null ratio. Null keeps
  every row. Constraints: at least 1 items; at most 5 items; at least 1 items; at most
  10 items.

Fields:
  column: string
      The column the test reads.
  op: one of eq|ne|lt|le|gt|ge|in|not_in|is_null|not_null
      The test. `eq` to `ge` compare each cell with `value`; `in` and `not_in` check it
      against a list; `is_null` and `not_null` read no value. No string matching or
      regex.
  value: true|false or integer or number or string or list of true|false or integer or number or string or null
      What the cells are tested against. One value for `eq` to `ge`, a list of up to 100
      for `in` and `not_in`, null for `is_null` and `not_null`. A numeric column takes
      numbers, a text column strings, a bool column bools; other columns take only
      `is_null` and `not_null`.
query-frame.mode:
mode: object or object or null, required
  Rows mode is `{"kind": "rows", "columns": [...], "limit": n, "order": {...}}`.
  `columns` null means every column, at most 10 returned; `limit` null means 20, at most
  50. `order` is `{"kind": "dataset"}` (the default), `{"kind": "random", "seed": n}`
  (null seed means a fixed default, so the same call draws the same rows) or `{"kind":
  "sort", "column": ..., "direction": "descending"}` (null direction means ascending;
  null and NaN cells last, ties in dataset order). Aggregate mode is `{"kind":
  "aggregate", "group_by": [...], "measures": [{"column": ..., "fn": ...}]}` with up to
  3 `group_by` columns (empty means one group of every matching row) and up to 5
  measures: `count`, `null_count`, `nunique`, and on numeric columns `sum`, `mean`,
  `std`, `min`, `max` and `median`. NaN counts as null. Null means rows mode with every
  default.

Variant 1 fields:
  kind: one of rows
      Always `rows`.
  columns: list of string, optional
      The columns to return, in this order. Null means every column. At most 10 are
      returned, the first 10 named; `omitted` counts the rest.
  limit: integer, optional
      Most rows to return, from 1 to 50. Null means 20. Constraints: at least 1; at most
      50.
  order: object or object or object or null
      Which matching rows to return: `dataset` takes the first, `random` a seeded
      sample, `sort` the top by one column.
      Fields: dataforge schema query-frame mode order

Variant 2 fields:
  kind: one of aggregate
      Always `aggregate`.
  group_by: list of string, optional
      Up to 3 key columns; each distinct combination of their values is a group, a null
      key included. Null or empty means the matching rows are one group. Constraints: at
      most 3 items.
  measures: list of object, optional
      Up to 5 measures, returned in this order within `measures` and `literal_measures`.
      Fields: dataforge schema query-frame mode measures
query-frame.mode.order:
mode.order: object or object or object or null, required
  Which matching rows to return: `dataset` takes the first, `random` a seeded sample,
  `sort` the top by one column. Null means `dataset`.

Variant 1 fields:
  kind: one of dataset
      Always `dataset`.

Variant 2 fields:
  kind: one of random
      Always `random`.
  seed: integer, optional
      Seed of the draw, from 0 to 4294967295. The same seed on the same frame and filter
      draws the same rows. Null means a fixed default. Constraints: at least 0; at most
      4294967295.

Variant 3 fields:
  kind: one of sort
      Always `sort`.
  column: string
      The column to sort by.
  direction: one of ascending|descending, optional
      `ascending` puts the smallest first, `descending` the largest. Null means
      `ascending`.
query-frame.mode.measures:
mode.measures: list of object, optional
  Up to 5 measures, returned in this order within `measures` and `literal_measures`.
  Null means none: only the group sizes. Constraints: at most 5 items.

Fields:
  column: string
      The column measured.
  fn: one of count|null_count|nunique|sum|mean|std|min|max|median
      `count` counts the cells that are not null, `null_count` those that are, `nunique`
      the distinct values that are not null. `sum`, `mean`, `std` (sample), `min`, `max`
      and `median` read numeric columns only and skip null cells. NaN counts as null.

resolve-recipe.routing:
routing: string, required
  A routing Handle, such as `routing_7f3a9c2e`.
resolve-recipe.hyperparameters:
hyperparameters: list of object, optional
  Hyperparameters you set, one entry per unit. Null keeps every resolved value.

Fields:
  unit_id: string
      The unit to tune, as `resolve_recipe` lists it: `mice`, `knn`, or
      `<strategy>:<column>` such as `mnar:income`.
  hyperparameters: object or object or object or object
      The record of the unit's strategy, picked by `kind`: `mice`, `knn`, `mnar` or
      `cluster_conditional`.
      Fields: dataforge schema resolve-recipe hyperparameters hyperparameters
resolve-recipe.hyperparameters.hyperparameters:
hyperparameters.hyperparameters: object or object or object or object, required
  The record of the unit's strategy, picked by `kind`: `mice`, `knn`, `mnar` or
  `cluster_conditional`. Only those strategies have hyperparameters. A null field keeps
  the resolved value.

Variant 1 fields:
  kind: one of mice
      Always `mice`.
  max_iter: integer, optional
      Most imputation rounds the block runs. Constraints: at least 1.
  tol: number, optional
      Convergence tolerance: the block stops once a round changes the fill by less than
      this. Constraints: at least 0.
  initial_strategy: one of mean|median, optional
      Which statistic fills missing cells before the first round.
  n_nearest_features: integer or one of all or null
      Most predictors each column's model reads, the most correlated first. `all` reads
      every active numeric column. Constraints: at least 1.

Variant 2 fields:
  kind: one of knn
      Always `knn`.
  n_neighbors: integer, optional
      Rows whose values fill a missing cell. A column with fewer donor rows uses them
      all. Constraints: at least 1.
  weights: one of uniform|distance, optional
      `distance` weighs nearer rows more; `uniform` weighs every neighbour the same.

Variant 3 fields:
  kind: one of mnar
      Always `mnar`.
  central_tendency: one of mean|median|mode, optional
      Which statistic the fill on record is. The column keeps its nulls either way.

Variant 4 fields:
  kind: one of cluster_conditional
      Always `cluster_conditional`.
  central_tendency: one of mean|median, optional
      Which statistic of its group fills a missing cell.
resolve-recipe.estimates:
estimates: list of object, optional
  Estimates you set, one entry per column. Null keeps every resolved estimate.

Fields:
  column: string
      The column, exactly as in the data. Its strategy must read estimates:
      `cluster_conditional` or `gmm_sampling`, or `knn` or `mice` on a
      `bounded_discrete` column.
  center1: number, optional
      First of the two mode centres a `cluster_conditional` or `gmm_sampling` column
      splits on. Null keeps the resolved value; when the column has none, set both
      centres.
  center2: number, optional
      Second mode centre. Null keeps the resolved value.
  feature_cols: list of string, optional
      Numeric columns a `cluster_conditional` column measures its cluster centroids
      over, replacing the resolved list. Null keeps the resolved list.
  domain_snap_bounds: object, optional
      The range a `bounded_discrete` column on `knn`, `mice` or `gmm_sampling` snaps its
      predictions into.
      Fields: dataforge schema resolve-recipe estimates domain_snap_bounds
resolve-recipe.estimates.domain_snap_bounds:
estimates.domain_snap_bounds: object, optional
  The range a `bounded_discrete` column on `knn`, `mice` or `gmm_sampling` snaps its
  predictions into. Null keeps the resolved range, the column's observed one.

Fields:
  low: number
      The smallest value a prediction may take.
  high: number
      The largest value a prediction may take. At least `low`.

route.profile:
profile: string, required
  A profile Handle, such as `profile_7f3a9c2e`.
route.strategies:
strategies: list of object, optional
  Strategies you set, one entry per column. Null means none.

Fields:
  column: string
      Column name, exactly as in the data.
  strategy: one of mean|median|mode|knn|mice|mnar|constant|dropped|passthrough|cluster_conditional|gmm_sampling
      The strategy. A column that is not numeric, or that profiling skipped, takes only
      `passthrough` or `dropped`. `indicator` is never declared: `mnar` adds the
      `<column>_missing` indicator itself.
  constant_fill: number, optional
      The fill value of a `constant` column, which needs one. Null for every other
      strategy.
  grouping_variable: string, optional
      For `cluster_conditional` only: the column whose groups the fill is taken within.
      Null takes it per mixture component instead.
route.default_strategy:
default_strategy: one of mean|median|mode|knn|mice|mnar|dropped|passthrough|cluster_conditional|gmm_sampling, optional
  The strategy every unlisted numeric column takes. Unlisted columns that are not
  numeric stay `passthrough`. Null routes every unlisted column from its profile.
route.model_choice:
model_choice: one of bayesian_ridge|random_forest_regressor|gradient_boosting_regressor, optional
  The estimator the MICE block trains with. Null lets the Estimator Ladder pick it from
  the block's nonlinearity. Setting it with no `mice` column fails.
route.exclude_columns:
exclude_columns: list of string, optional
  Columns to leave out of this and every later phase, added to what the profile already
  excludes. Null means none.
route.skip_columns:
skip_columns: list of string, optional
  Columns routing leaves as they are: `passthrough` with reason `soft_excluded`, and
  never a predictor. Null means none.
route.thresholds:
thresholds: object, optional
  Dials, grouped by what they judge, each with its default and range. Null keeps every
  default.

Fields:
  numeric: object, optional
      The Feasibility Floor, the Signal Score and the bimodal rules.
      Fields: dataforge schema route thresholds numeric
route.thresholds.numeric:
thresholds.numeric: object, optional
  The Feasibility Floor, the Signal Score and the bimodal rules.

Fields:
  knn_max_rows: integer, optional
      KNN's Resource Ceiling: most rows a frame may have for a column to take `knn`.
      Null means 50000. Constraints: at least 1.
  mice_min_rows_per_predictor: number, optional
      The Feasibility Floor: fewest non-missing rows per predictor a column needs to
      take `mice`. Null means 2. Constraints: at least 0.
  mice_max_nearest_features: integer, optional
      Most predictors the Feasibility Floor counts for `mice`. Null means 20.
      Constraints: at least 1.
  mice_correlation_threshold: number, optional
      Least absolute correlation for a column to count as a predictor in the Signal
      Score's breadth. Null means 0.1. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  signal_score_breadth_weight: number, optional
      How much the count of predictors may add to the Signal Score. Null means 0.1.
      Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  signal_score_latent_weight: number, optional
      How far mutual information alone can raise the Signal Score. Null means 0.3.
      Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  signal_score_middle_tier_min: number, optional
      Signal Score at or above which a column may take a model (`knn` first). Must not
      exceed `signal_score_top_tier_min`. Null means 0.3. Constraints: at least 0; at
      most 1.
  signal_score_top_tier_min: number, optional
      Signal Score at or above which a column takes the richest feasible model (`mice`
      first). Null means 0.6. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  bimodal_min_correlated_features: integer, optional
      Fewest correlated columns a bimodal column needs to try a model instead of
      `cluster_conditional`. Null means 3. Constraints: at least 1.
  bimodal_correlation_threshold: number, optional
      Least absolute correlation for a column to count toward
      `bimodal_min_correlated_features`. Null means 0.2. Constraints: at least 0; at
      most 1.

split.profile:
profile: string, required
  A profile Handle, such as `profile_7f3a9c2e`. Its frame is split.
split.scheme:
scheme: object or object or object or object or object or object or object or object or object or null, required
  How to split, chosen by `kind`; null means `profile_stratified` with its defaults.

Variant 1 fields:
  kind: one of random
      Always `random`.
  test_size: number, optional
      Share of rows held out as `test`. Null means 0.2. Constraints: greater than 0;
      less than 1.
  stratify: true|false, optional
      True keeps each target class's share the same in train and test. Null stratifies
      when the profile declares a target.
  target: string, optional
      The declared target to stratify on. Null takes the profile's target; name one when
      it declares several.

Variant 2 fields:
  kind: one of time
      Always `time`.
  time_column: string
      The datetime or numeric column that orders the rows. Its sentinels count as
      missing, and rows with no time go to train.
  test_size: number, optional
      Share of rows, the latest ones, held out as `test`. Null means 0.2 unless `cutoff`
      is set; set at most one of the two. Constraints: greater than 0; less than 1.
  cutoff: string or number or null
      Rows at or after this time are `test`. A datetime for a datetime column (an ISO
      string on the CLI), a number for a numeric one. Null splits by `test_size`.
      Constraints: in date-time format.

Variant 3 fields:
  kind: one of group
      Always `group`.
  group_column: string
      The column naming each row's group, such as a customer id. Rows missing it form
      one group.
  test_size: number, optional
      Share of groups held out as `test`. Null means 0.2. Constraints: greater than 0;
      less than 1.

Variant 4 fields:
  kind: one of kfold
      Always `kfold`.
  k: integer, optional
      Number of folds. Null means 5. Constraints: at least 2; at most 100.
  stratify: true|false, optional
      True keeps each target class's share the same in every fold. Null stratifies when
      the profile declares a target.
  target: string, optional
      The declared target to stratify on. Null takes the profile's target; name one when
      it declares several.

Variant 5 fields:
  kind: one of group_kfold
      Always `group_kfold`.
  group_column: string
      The column naming each row's group. Rows missing it form one group.
  k: integer, optional
      Number of folds, at most the number of groups. Null means 5. Constraints: at least
      2; at most 100.
  stratify: true|false, optional
      True balances target classes across folds as far as whole groups allow. Null
      stratifies when the profile declares a target.
  target: string, optional
      The declared target to stratify on. Null takes the profile's target; name one when
      it declares several.

Variant 6 fields:
  kind: one of repeated_kfold
      Always `repeated_kfold`.
  k: integer, optional
      Number of folds per repeat. Null means 5. Constraints: at least 2; at most 100.
  repeats: integer, optional
      Number of repeats. `k * repeats` may be at most 100. Null means 10. Constraints:
      at least 1; at most 50.
  stratify: true|false, optional
      True keeps each target class's share the same in every fold. Null stratifies when
      the profile declares a target.
  target: string, optional
      The declared target to stratify on. Null takes the profile's target; name one when
      it declares several.

Variant 7 fields:
  kind: one of holdout_cv
      Always `holdout_cv`.
  test_size: number, optional
      Share of rows held out as `test`. Null means 0.2. Constraints: greater than 0;
      less than 1.
  k: integer, optional
      Number of folds over the rest. Null means 5. Constraints: at least 2; at most 100.
  stratify: true|false, optional
      True stratifies the hold-out and the folds on the target. Null stratifies when the
      profile declares a target.
  target: string, optional
      The declared target to stratify on. Null takes the profile's target; name one when
      it declares several.

Variant 8 fields:
  kind: one of profile_stratified
      Always `profile_stratified`.
  test_size: number, optional
      Share of rows held out as `test`. It also sets the viability floor, `ceil(2 /
      min(test_size, 1 - test_size))` rows. Null means 0.2. Constraints: greater than 0;
      less than 1.
  target: string, optional
      The declared target to balance with the other signals. Null takes the profile's
      target, if any; name one when it declares several.

Variant 9 fields:
  kind: one of profile_stratified_kfold
      Always `profile_stratified_kfold`.
  k: integer, optional
      Number of folds. It is also the viability floor, in rows. Null means 5.
      Constraints: at least 2; at most 100.
  target: string, optional
      The declared target to balance with the other signals. Null takes the profile's
      target, if any; name one when it declares several.
split.seed:
seed: integer, optional
  Seed of every shuffle. Null means a fixed default, so the same call gives the same
  split. Constraints: at least 0; at most 4294967295.
split.thresholds:
thresholds: object, optional
  Dials of the profile-stratified schemes, each with its default and range. Null keeps
  every default.

Fields:
  stratification: object, optional
      The signal gates of the profile-stratified schemes.
      Fields: dataforge schema split thresholds stratification
split.thresholds.stratification:
thresholds.stratification: object, optional
  The signal gates of the profile-stratified schemes.

Fields:
  max_stratification_signals: integer, optional
      Most signals balanced at once. The cap is the smaller of this and `n_rows /
      rows_per_signal`. Null means 50. Constraints: at least 1.
  rows_per_signal: integer, optional
      Rows the data must have per balanced signal. Null means 10. Constraints: at least
      1.
  boolean_minority_threshold: number, optional
      A boolean column whose rarer value is below this share becomes a signal. Null
      means 0.05. Constraints: at most 0.5; greater than 0.
  redundancy_correlation_threshold: number, optional
      Absolute correlation at or above which two signals count as one, and the less
      important is dropped. Null means 0.95. Constraints: at most 1; greater than 0.

  100.
